world_runner.anel.01.intro: a windmill keeper who has never once run with a tailwind by choice
world_runner.anel.02.intro: reads wind the way other runners read splits
world_runner.anel.03.intro: plans every race around the forecast and is right about it
world_runner.anel.04.intro: a mill mechanic with an unnerving sense of when to move
world_runner.anel.05.intro: races only on the windiest days and skips the calm ones
world_runner.anel.06.intro: the tallest runner on the continent and the worst possible shape for it
world_runner.anel.07.intro: has won exactly once doing this and considers it settled
world_runner.anel.08.intro: entirely open about the tactic and unapologetic
world_runner.anel.09.intro: a sailmaker, and she races the way she trims
world_runner.anel.10.intro: says he has never chosen wrong and the record supports him
world_runner.anel.11.intro: the only runner here who treats a headwind as an opportunity
world_runner.anel.12.intro: has finished in the top ten of every race he has ever entered
world_runner.anel.13.intro: the field describes racing her as running in a storm, twice
world_runner.anel.14.intro: a weather-watcher who spends his working life waiting
world_runner.anel.15.intro: has calculated the cost exactly and finds it worth paying
world_runner.anel.16.intro: ran his first race at sixty and has not missed one since
world_runner.anel.17.intro: the fastest final third on the continent and no patience for the first two
world_runner.hora.01.intro: a mirror-ruin surveyor who knows which panels hold
world_runner.hora.02.intro: the most heat-adapted runner in the world and entirely undramatic about it
world_runner.hora.03.intro: plans every race around where the ruins throw shade
world_runner.hora.04.intro: has finished second more times than anyone and is still trying
world_runner.hora.05.intro: a glass-walker, and the surface that frightens the field is his home
world_runner.hora.06.intro: started racing to escape a job and stayed for the heat
world_runner.hora.07.intro: has explained why several times and nobody has been convinced
world_runner.hora.08.intro: the field calls it hiding and she calls it thinking
world_runner.hora.09.intro: grew up racing between the mirror walls where there is no straight line
world_runner.hora.10.intro: will not say who until afterwards, and sometimes not then
world_runner.hora.11.intro: a heat-haze forecaster who races on the days he predicts worst
world_runner.hora.12.intro: has never dropped a place in the second half of any race, ever
world_runner.hora.13.intro: says the desert already changes constantly and he is only matching it
world_runner.hora.14.intro: a silica spinner, and the quietest person in the field by a margin
world_runner.hora.15.intro: has cut her feet twice and does not intend to a third time
world_runner.hora.16.intro: the shortest route through Hora belongs to him and always has
world_runner.hora.17.intro: a night runner forced into daylight racing and getting used to it
world_runner.kael.01.intro: a bridge rigger, and the wobble does not register for her
world_runner.kael.02.intro: has crossed every bridge in the archipelago at full speed
world_runner.kael.03.intro: plans races island by island, out loud, to anyone nearby
world_runner.kael.04.intro: the most anticlimactic first hour and the fastest last ten minutes
world_runner.kael.05.intro: the field has stopped following and she keeps doing it
world_runner.kael.06.intro: a route surveyor who has measured all of it personally
world_runner.kael.07.intro: has done this eleven times and won twice, which she says is enough
world_runner.kael.08.intro: openly frightened of the height and races anyway, every time
world_runner.kael.09.intro: grew up on a tether and treats corners as free distance
world_runner.kael.10.intro: says the archipelago is too dangerous to race alone and means it
world_runner.kael.11.intro: a wind-reader who knows exactly when the crossings calm
world_runner.kael.12.intro: has finished every race he has entered, which nobody else here can say
world_runner.kael.13.intro: says predictability on a rope bridge is how people fall
world_runner.kael.14.intro: a tether-maker, and he trusts his own work absolutely
world_runner.kael.15.intro: inspects the bridges professionally and races the safe side
world_runner.kael.16.intro: the fastest line across the archipelago and it belongs to him
world_runner.kael.17.intro: races twice a year, wins one, and is unbothered about the other
world_runner.lumena.01.intro: kept the citadel wall for thirty years and only started racing at forty
world_runner.lumena.02.intro: archivist who memorised every split ever recorded on this course
world_runner.lumena.03.intro: lamp-lighter who has run the same route before dawn since childhood
world_runner.lumena.04.intro: former bell-ringer, counts the whole race in fours
world_runner.lumena.05.intro: the only runner in Lumena who has done both, in consecutive years
world_runner.lumena.06.intro: refuses to race on the inside after a fall she will not discuss
world_runner.lumena.07.intro: stonemason, built the ramp the race starts on
world_runner.lumena.08.intro: runs to have somewhere to talk, and is annoyed to be good at it
world_runner.lumena.09.intro: trained as a chorister, hears the field breathing out of time
world_runner.lumena.10.intro: a night-shift medic who runs on four hours of sleep and prefers it
world_runner.lumena.11.intro: was a message runner between the ramparts before there were races
world_runner.lumena.12.intro: keeps a written record of every place she has finished in, since she was nine
world_runner.lumena.13.intro: a quiet man who has never given an interview
world_runner.lumena.14.intro: gilder by trade, describes the last third of a race as the part worth doing
world_runner.lumena.15.intro: lost the continental title by a hundredth and has not mentioned it since
world_runner.lumena.16.intro: the pace-setter every Lumena runner learned to hate and then imitate
world_runner.lumena.17.intro: nobody in the citadel knows what he does when he is not racing
world_runner.neris.01.intro: an archive diver who is entirely comfortable at depth
world_runner.neris.02.intro: has never varied a split by more than two seconds in her life
world_runner.neris.03.intro: reads pressure gradients the way other runners read hills
world_runner.neris.04.intro: the field knows exactly what he will do and cannot prevent it
world_runner.neris.05.intro: a salvage runner who treats water as an ally
world_runner.neris.06.intro: the longest sustained effort anyone here has recorded
world_runner.neris.07.intro: has won this way exactly once and considers it proof
world_runner.neris.08.intro: a pressure engineer, and he does the arithmetic constantly
world_runner.neris.09.intro: trained in the spiral and has never lost a metre in one
world_runner.neris.10.intro: does not consider this tactics, only company
world_runner.neris.11.intro: a lume-thread weaver with an unusual sense of timing
world_runner.neris.12.intro: has raced here for nineteen years and improved every one of them
world_runner.neris.13.intro: says the depths already do this and he is being consistent
world_runner.neris.14.intro: nobody has heard her breathe in a race and it unsettles people
world_runner.neris.15.intro: lost a season to a collapsed section and now checks everything
world_runner.neris.16.intro: the shortest route through the archive and he found it first
world_runner.neris.17.intro: a quiet former record-holder who races for the hall section alone
world_runner.nival.01.intro: a ridge warden who has done this for other people for twenty years
world_runner.nival.02.intro: the most technically consistent runner on the continent
world_runner.nival.03.intro: reads wind chill the way others read a split
world_runner.nival.04.intro: a rescue volunteer who is very hard to hurry
world_runner.nival.05.intro: runs best when the conditions are worst and knows it
world_runner.nival.06.intro: holds the continental long-distance record and does not mention it
world_runner.nival.07.intro: has been rescued once and it has changed nothing
world_runner.nival.08.intro: entirely open that this is the correct thing to do
world_runner.nival.09.intro: grew up on the ridge and has never run on flat ground
world_runner.nival.10.intro: has never once been shaken off, in any race
world_runner.nival.11.intro: a snow forecaster with a very specific kind of patience
world_runner.nival.12.intro: sixty-one, and has beaten every age group she has ever been in
world_runner.nival.13.intro: says the ridge does the same and he is only being honest
world_runner.nival.14.intro: the field describes her as a shadow with better footing
world_runner.nival.15.intro: lost a friend to a cornice and will not go near one
world_runner.nival.16.intro: the boldest line on the continent and she has never fallen
world_runner.nival.17.intro: a former champion who now paces others and still finishes top five
world_runner.origin.01.intro: the first runner to complete the worldline course, and he will not discuss it
world_runner.origin.02.intro: a rift surveyor whose job is to notice when the ground disagrees
world_runner.origin.03.intro: has mapped which sections are which and shares the map freely
world_runner.origin.04.intro: the most patient runner in the world by a considerable margin
world_runner.origin.05.intro: says the seams are the only interesting part of the course
world_runner.origin.06.intro: holds the fastest recorded time on the Apex Axis approach
world_runner.origin.07.intro: has finished first once and last four times, and prefers the story
world_runner.origin.08.intro: entirely rational about a course that is not
world_runner.origin.09.intro: the turns are where the geometry stops working and she likes it
world_runner.origin.10.intro: says nobody should be alone in there and does something about it
world_runner.origin.11.intro: a fracture analyst who knows exactly where the ground settles
world_runner.origin.12.intro: has started last, deliberately, in every race for six years
world_runner.origin.13.intro: has a theory about this that nobody has managed to disprove
world_runner.origin.14.intro: the only person who has run the Axis approach without a light
world_runner.origin.15.intro: has never taken a risk in a race and has never failed to finish
world_runner.origin.16.intro: the shortest and worst line through Origin, and it is his
world_runner.origin.17.intro: races once a year, at the Axis, and has never been beaten there
world_runner.rubra.01.intro: a furnace hand who considers the race the cool part of the day
world_runner.rubra.02.intro: holds the continental record for consistency and none for speed
world_runner.rubra.03.intro: reads the canyon shadow like a course map, because it is one
world_runner.rubra.04.intro: the most patient runner in Rubra and by some distance the least popular
world_runner.rubra.05.intro: a slag-hauler with an engine for a chest and no tactical sense at all
world_runner.rubra.06.intro: ran her first race to prove a point and has not stopped
world_runner.rubra.07.intro: has finished first and last in the same event, a year apart
world_runner.rubra.08.intro: the smallest runner on the continent and entirely unembarrassed by it
world_runner.rubra.09.intro: grew up running messages down the canyon and never learned to brake
world_runner.rubra.10.intro: keeps a list, and everyone on the continent knows they are on it
world_runner.rubra.11.intro: a kiln master who understands exactly what temperature does to a person
world_runner.rubra.12.intro: has never led a race before the final kilometre and has won six
world_runner.rubra.13.intro: openly says he would rather ruin a race than lose a slow one
world_runner.rubra.14.intro: the quietest runner in the field and the one nobody wants behind them
world_runner.rubra.15.intro: lost two toenails to the inside line and made a decision
world_runner.rubra.16.intro: the only Rubra runner to lead a race from the gun and finish first
world_runner.rubra.17.intro: a former champion who now races twice a year and is still the favourite
world_runner.serene.01.intro: grew up on the planks and does not look down, ever
world_runner.serene.02.intro: a bridge inspector, and it shows in his footing
world_runner.serene.03.intro: times every race to the tide table and has never been wrong
world_runner.serene.04.intro: a net-mender with an hour of patience and thirty seconds of speed
world_runner.serene.05.intro: the only runner who genuinely prefers the boards soaked
world_runner.serene.06.intro: a lighthouse keeper who counts in hours, not minutes
world_runner.serene.07.intro: has never finished worse than fifth doing something everyone calls stupid
world_runner.serene.08.intro: openly hates the cold and races anyway
world_runner.serene.09.intro: a dock runner, and the corners are the part she trains
world_runner.serene.10.intro: says he only needs to beat one person and he is usually right
world_runner.serene.11.intro: a swimmer first, and it is visible in how little the wet bothers her
world_runner.serene.12.intro: started running at forty-eight and has beaten people half his age
world_runner.serene.13.intro: accused of ruining races, and has said she intends to
world_runner.serene.14.intro: a phosphor diver used to holding his breath and his tongue
world_runner.serene.15.intro: fell once at nineteen and has run wide every race since
world_runner.serene.16.intro: the shortest line through Serene, and he has never given it up
world_runner.serene.17.intro: a night fisher who races before sleeping and after working
world_runner.tempora.01.intro: a clockmaster who announces his splits before the race and hits them
world_runner.tempora.02.intro: the most literal runner on the continent and proud of it
world_runner.tempora.03.intro: has explained the arithmetic to anyone who will listen
world_runner.tempora.04.intro: a bell-keeper who understands exactly when a thing must happen
world_runner.tempora.05.intro: the course has hour markers because she asked for them
world_runner.tempora.06.intro: describes himself as a mainspring and nobody has corrected him
world_runner.tempora.07.intro: has done this every race for eleven years and won three
world_runner.tempora.08.intro: says leading is a waste of a resource and he is not wrong
world_runner.tempora.09.intro: a courier through the clockwork district, corners are her commute
world_runner.tempora.10.intro: names the rival in advance, which they universally hate
world_runner.tempora.11.intro: has a written plan and follows it exactly, including the losses
world_runner.tempora.12.intro: sixty-four, and she has done this in every race for a decade
world_runner.tempora.13.intro: says a fortress running on borrowed time should not keep to one
world_runner.tempora.14.intro: a movement assembler used to very small, very quiet work
world_runner.tempora.15.intro: turned an ankle at twenty-two and has run wide ever since
world_runner.tempora.16.intro: has led every race she has entered and finished most of them
world_runner.tempora.17.intro: a former champion who now races only when the timing amuses him
world_runner.verdia.01.intro: grew up on the canopy walkways and finds flat ground unsettling
world_runner.verdia.02.intro: forest surveyor, has walked every metre of this course at least twice
world_runner.verdia.03.intro: a botanist who treats the first half as data collection
world_runner.verdia.04.intro: the youngest continental medallist Verdia has produced
world_runner.verdia.05.intro: runs bent forward from habit and never straightened up
world_runner.verdia.06.intro: tends the sap channels, works in hour-long blocks, races in them too
world_runner.verdia.07.intro: has won this way twice and lost this way nine times, and is unmoved
world_runner.verdia.08.intro: a woodcutter with a runner build he did not ask for
world_runner.verdia.09.intro: the only person who has raced the spore season five years running
world_runner.verdia.10.intro: will tell you exactly who he is racing and it is never the leader
world_runner.verdia.11.intro: a mycologist who describes racing in terms of networks
world_runner.verdia.12.intro: started running at fifty-one because the walk to work was too short
world_runner.verdia.13.intro: says a steady pace is a decision to stop thinking
world_runner.verdia.14.intro: a tracker, and he does not consider this a metaphor
world_runner.verdia.15.intro: lost a season to a collision and now pays the extra distance gladly
world_runner.verdia.16.intro: the shortest route through Verdia is his and he knows it
world_runner.verdia.17.intro: a bloomfall weaver who races three times a year and wins one
world_runner.voltis.01.intro: a line technician who runs the route she inspects
world_runner.voltis.02.intro: says the city is full of rhythm and most people ignore it
world_runner.voltis.03.intro: a grounding engineer with an unusual amount of patience
world_runner.voltis.04.intro: the field has learned to watch her and it has not helped
world_runner.voltis.05.intro: a smelter hand who trains in ninety-second intervals because his shift does
world_runner.voltis.06.intro: holds the longest unbroken sequence of finishes on the continent
world_runner.voltis.07.intro: has been told to stop doing this by three separate coaches
world_runner.voltis.08.intro: small, quiet, and consistently in the top ten
world_runner.voltis.09.intro: a courier before the races existed and unchanged since
world_runner.voltis.10.intro: chooses the person she thinks will win and is right about half the time
world_runner.voltis.11.intro: a cable rigger with legs built for exactly one thing
world_runner.voltis.12.intro: has never been in the lead before the last kilometre of anything
world_runner.voltis.13.intro: has said the point is to make the race unpleasant, and means it
world_runner.voltis.14.intro: a signal operator, used to watching one thing for a very long time
world_runner.voltis.15.intro: lost a shoe to a rail groove and made a permanent decision
world_runner.voltis.16.intro: the most aggressive first kilometre in Voltis and she is fifty-three
world_runner.voltis.17.intro: a former champion who now races once a year and is still dangerous
